_howto: GitHub repositories the Library shows. Hand-picked: nothing appears
unless it is listed here.
At build time CI reads each one from the GitHub API and publishes a
snapshot beside the page (repos.generated.json): description, language,
stars, last push, the latest CI run on the default branch, and the latest
release. The browser never calls GitHub - visitors would share the
anonymous limit of 60 requests an hour, and a token cannot be shipped to
a public page. The snapshot is refreshed daily.
REPO shape - only 'repo' is required:
"repo":  "fvtale/DocShift",
"entry": "/docshift/",
"label": "DocShift",
"allowPrivate": false
'entry' attaches the details to the library row with that path. Without
it the repository is listed in its own On GitHub section instead. One
repository per row.
PRIVATE REPOSITORIES are refused unless 'allowPrivate' is true on that
item. Listing one publishes its name, language, last push and CI status on
a public page, so it has to be a decision rather than a typo. Reading one
also needs the LIBRARY_READ_TOKEN secret: the workflow's own token can
only see this repository. Links to a private repository are not shown,
since they would 404 for everyone else.
If any listed repository cannot be read, the build fails and nothing is
published: the live page stays as it was rather than losing rows.
